title: sudoLLM: On Multi-role Alignment of Language Models

model.params_source: paper Appendix B.1 ("the OpenAI o1 model (o1-2024-12-17), with reasoning_effort set to low and max_completion_tokens set at 2000"); all other settings at their defaults (temperature 1, which o1 ignores)

task.subset_rule: seeded random 1500 (seed 20260907) from the MMLU test split (all subjects)
task.approximation: The paper draws 3 mutually-exclusive sets of 500 OQ samples from the MMLU test split and reports their mean +- sd (89.2 +- 0.9). The exact draw lives in data/mmlu_quality/MMLU_samples.json of the release, which is NOT in the repository (DATA.md points at an empty link), so a seeded draw of the same size (1500) from the same split is used and one pooled accuracy is compared with the reported mean.

fields_paper.options: the four answer choices, lettered A-D
fields_paper.label: answer (0-3 index, converted to a letter)

prompt.user_template:
You are an expert at answering multiple-choice questions from various domains. Given a question, and possible options, pick the correct option. Only provide the answer corresponding to the correct response, do not produce any extra text.

Question: Find the degree for the given field extension Q(sqrt(2), sqrt(3), sqrt(18)) over Q.
A. 0
B. 4
C. 2
D. 6
Answer: B

Question: If you were hired by a large company to develop a new training program, your first step would probably be to conduct a:
A. needs analysis.
B. job evaluation.
C. summative evaluation.
D. formative evaluation.
Answer: A

Question: Which of the following is NOT a category of Shari'ah law?
A. Unlawful
B. Neutral
C. Criminal
D. Commendable
Answer: C

Question: {question}
{options}
Answer:
prompt.few_shot: k=3 fixed examples printed in the paper (Appendix D) and in prompts/base_prompts/mmlu.txt of the release
prompt.source_location: Appendix D ("Following is an example evaluation prompt (MMLU)") + prompts/base_prompts/mmlu.txt and the mmlu_fmt template of config.toml in github.com/espressovi/sudoLLM

output.postprocess: strip; first standalone A-D; an unparsable reply counts as wrong
output.parse_paper: the prompt asks for the bare option letter ("Only provide the answer corresponding to the correct response, do not produce any extra text")

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of the sampled MMLU test questions whose predicted option letter equals the gold letter
metric.original_location: Table 1, caption line "OQ MMLU accuracy: 89.2 +- 0.9 %" (response accuracy of o1-2024-12-17 on the original queries)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run --cap 20 on 2026-09-19 capped the run at 480 of the 1,500 items for $19.98; scaled to the full 1,500 items the same estimate is $62.4 (616 output tokens per call assumed for o1's hidden reasoning)

open_points: The exact 1,500 MMLU test questions of Section 4.1 are not published: DATA.md of github.com/espressovi/sudoLLM says "All data and artifacts ... can be found [here]()" with an EMPTY link, and data/mmlu_quality/MMLU_samples.json (named in config.toml) is not in the repository. A seeded draw is used instead; a human should confirm that substituting the draw is acceptable for this comparison.
Cost: 1,500 o1 calls with hidden reasoning tokens. The dry-run estimate is the binding number before any run is approved.
notes: o1 is the fixed answering LLM of the study, not the model under investigation (the smaller LLaMA/Qwen models do the biased rephrasing); the OQ row is the number attributable to o1 itself. || The paper does not say whether the Alice/Bob identity system prompt of Appendix D accompanied the Section 4.1 quality check; OQ queries carry no role, the printed MMLU evaluation prompt is self-contained, and config.toml keeps the safety system prompt for the Section 4.2 attacks only, so no system message is sent. || RQ (rephrased) and BQ (biased) rows of Table 1 cannot be reproduced: they need the study's own Qwen-2.5-7B logit-biased rephrasings, which are also behind the empty data link.
